reconcile.note: Fausset and his co-authors read Luke's general term 'apostles' in Acts 9:27 as satisfied by the two individuals Paul names in Galatians 1:18-19, Peter and James.

discrepancy.note: Cassels argues Acts' open mingling with the apostles directly contradicts Paul's sworn statement that he saw only Peter and James.

quotes.text: Paul was with them coming in and going out at Jerusalem, preaching boldly in the name of the Lord. Here again the declaration of Paul is explicit, and distinctly contradicts this story both in the letter and the spirit. He makes no mention of Barnabas. He states that he went to Jerusalem specially with the view of making the acquaintance of Peter, with whom he remained fifteen days…we have here the emphatic assurance that, in addition to Peter, Paul saw no one except "James, the Lord's brother."
quotes.attr: Walter Richard Cassels (d. 1907), Supernatural Religion, Vol. III (1879), on Acts 9:27 and Galatians 1:19.

sides.snippet: Barnabas took him, and brought him to the apostles
sides.verseText: But Barnabas took him, and brought him to the apostles, and declared to them how he had seen the Lord in the way, and that he had spoken to him, and how at Damascus he had preached boldly in the name of Jesus.

sides.snippet: But of the other apostles I saw no one, except James, the Lord's brother.
sides.verseText: But of the other apostles I saw no one, except James, the Lord's brother.
